title: Hierarchical Prefetching: A Software-Hardware Instruction Prefetcher for Server Applications
problem: Server-side applications have large instruction working sets that cause severe front-end bottlenecks even with state-of-the-art fetch-directed instruction prefetching (FDIP), because record-and-replay prefetchers lose coverage and timeliness when actual control flow diverges from predicted control flow.
motivation: Instruction cache misses are a primary bottleneck in modern server workloads (databases, web servers, key-value stores), and existing prefetchers fail when control flow variability causes mismatches between recorded and replayed sequences.
method: The system analyzes the server binary to identify larger functional code regions called Bundles (10s–100s of kilobytes) that tend to execute together. Hardware then uses a record-and-replay prefetcher that watches which Bundles are executed and replays that pattern, prefetching entire Bundles when their entry points are detected rather than individual cache lines. Bundle metadata lives mostly in main memory with under 2KB stored on-chip to save space. This approach tolerates control flow variability because prefetching entire functional regions works even when execution takes unexpected paths that would defeat line-by-line prediction.
key_novelty: The core idea is defining large functional code Bundles (10s–100s kilobytes) and prefetching them as complete units rather than individual cache lines, so that execution stays on track even when control flow diverges from predictions.
contributions: Bundle abstraction: coarse-grained functionality blocks identified via software analysis for server code
Hierarchical prefetching microarchitecture combining software Bundle formation with lightweight hardware record-and-replay under 2KB on-chip storage
6.6% average IPC improvement over FDIP across 11 server workloads
Improved miss coverage and timeliness over prior instruction prefetchers under control flow variability

metrics.speedup: 6.6% average performance gain over FDIP across 11 server workloads

limitations: Software analysis for Bundle formation must be performed offline per binary; effectiveness on highly dynamic or JIT-compiled server code not discussed.
primary_theme: Coarse-grained hierarchical instruction prefetching for server front-end bottlenecks
